title: Age Limits for Scholarships and PhDs in Europe: The Honest List for 2027
seoTitle: Age Limits: Scholarships & PhD in Europe (2027 Honest List)
seoDescription: Which scholarships have age limits in 2027: Türkiye (21/30/35), Swiss (35), Eiffel (25/30), MEXT (35) — and which PhD routes have none at all. The full list.
intro: Employed European PhDs have no age limits; a specific list of government scholarships does. The honest 2027 list, programme by programme.
description: Age limits for European scholarships and PhD positions in 2027: which programmes cap age and which have no limit.
author: NextApply Team
excerpt: Which scholarships cap age in 2027 — and which PhD routes ignore age entirely.
content:
"Am I too old for this?" is the most-asked, least-answered question in international education — and the honest answer splits the world in two. European doctoral employment has no age limits at all: hire a 45-year-old researcher and the university pays the same scale, the same pension, the same parental leave. But a specific, well-known list of government scholarships does carry hard age ceilings, written into eligibility rules and checked at screening. Knowing which world each door belongs to changes everything about how you plan.

The programmes with real age limits

ProgrammeAge limit
Türkiye Bursları — bachelor’sUnder 21
Türkiye Bursları — master’sUnder 30
Türkiye Bursları — PhDUnder 35
Swiss Government ExcellenceUnder 35
France Excellence Eiffel — master’s25 or under
France Excellence Eiffel — PhD30 or under
MEXT (Japan) — research studentsUnder 35
Stipendium HungaricumNo universal limit
Erasmus Mundus Joint MastersNo limit (consortia may set preferences)
European PhD positions (DE, NL, Nordics, CH)No limit — employment law applies
UKRI-funded UK studentshipsNo limit

Three patterns explain why these specific programmes set ceilings. Government talent-pipeline schemes — Türkiye Bursları, MEXT, the Swiss Excellence awards — invest in careers they expect to span decades, so they select early. Eiffel’s master’s ceiling exists because the programme explicitly targets pre-career candidates. And everywhere a limit appears, it applies at application, checked against identity documents at the first screening — there are no rounding sympathies, and being 30 years and 4 months old is a rejection at a "under 30" scheme regardless of everything else in the file.

[[chart:age-ceilings]]

The world without limits

Employed doctoral positions — the German TV-L contracts, Dutch employment PhDs, Nordic salaried positions, Swiss assistantships — are jobs, and European employment law does not let universities discriminate by age. A 38-year-old software engineer starting an IMPRS doctorate, a 42-year-old teacher beginning a Danish PhD, a 50-year-old professional enrolling for an Italian dottorato: all normal, all funded identically. The same holds for UKRI studentships in the UK and most university-specific scholarships. Foundation funding (Kone in Finland, the German foundations) and Marie Curie doctoral networks also carry no general age bar.

Why the split matters strategically: the capped scholarships and the unlimited employment routes pay on different scales, and the capped ones are not automatically richer. Türkiye Bursları’s PhD stipend converts to roughly €320 a month; a German TV-L E13 contract pays four times that after tax. The age ceiling at a scholarship is therefore also a signal about its nature — a talent investment rather than employment — and applicants who internalise that distinction stop mourning capped schemes and start out-earning them through the uncapped system, as our net-pay comparison makes concrete.

Strategy for the over-30 applicant

  • Aim the employment route first. German, Dutch, Nordic and Swiss positions ignore age entirely — and pay better than most capped scholarships anyway. Our net-pay comparison shows the trade.
  • Check the scholarship list ruthlessly. If you are 31, Türkiye’s PhD track and the Swiss Excellence award remain open (under 35); Eiffel’s doctoral track does not (30 max) — plan in months, not vibes.
  • Reframe the CV, not the birthday. The question committees actually ask is whether you are competitive now: recent output beats youth. Our gap-explaining guide handles the narrative.
  • For master’s applicants over 30: Europe’s universities admit freely; the constraint is scholarships — Hungaricum, Erasmus Mundus and university awards mostly carry no limit, while Eiffel-style pipelines do.

The funded, no-age-limit positions below — employed contracts in Germany, the Netherlands and the Nordics — are where career-changers land best.
